segments.say: Now let's take a slow, gentle journey through the body, from the top of your head all the way down to your feet. There's nothing to fix along the way, and nothing to get right. We're just visiting, one place at a time, the way you might walk slowly through a quiet house at night, turning off the lights room by room.

Start at the very top of your head. Imagine a gentle warmth resting there, like the soft light of a lamp. Let it spread slowly across your scalp, loosening any small tightness you didn't know was there. Nothing to do. Just let the warmth arrive, and let the top of your head feel heavy and calm.

Let that warmth drift down to your forehead. So often, without noticing, we hold a little frown there, a small crease of concentration from a long day of thinking. Let it smooth out now. Imagine the skin of your forehead becoming wide and soft and easy, like still water on a windless night.

Now let the softness move through the rest of your face. Let your eyes rest heavy in their sockets, the eyelids loose. Let your cheeks relax. Let your jaw drop just a little, so your teeth part. And let your tongue rest gently in your mouth, not pressing anywhere. Your whole face can let go now. It doesn't need to show anything to anyone.

Feel the back of your neck, where it meets the pillow. All day, it has held up your head, turning to look at things, nodding, leaning toward screens and pages and people. Now it doesn't need to hold anything. The pillow is doing that for it. Let the neck grow long and soft, fully supported, fully at rest.

Now the shoulders. They're often where the day collects, quietly, like snow on a roof. Breathe in, and as you breathe out, let them drop. Just a little. Then, on the next breath out, a little more. Let them sink down and away from your ears, heavy and warm, settling into the bed beneath you.

Let that heaviness flow down your arms. The upper arms, the elbows, the forearms. Imagine them growing so heavy that lifting them would take a great deal of effort, and there's no reason at all to try. They can simply lie where they are, still and warm, resting on the bed or the blanket like a sleeping cat.

Here's a small reminder as we go. The body knows how to rest. You've done this every single night of your life, mostly without thinking about it at all. Tonight, you're simply giving it a little company along the way. A kind attention, room by room, as everything grows quiet.

show.text: The body knows how to rest.

segments.say: Now the hands. Let your fingers uncurl, if they've been holding on to anything. Let your palms rest open, or turned down, whatever feels easiest. Notice the warmth in your fingertips. Hands work so hard for us, all day long. They've earned this rest. Let them be soft and loose and completely still.

Let your attention move to your chest. Feel it rising gently with each breath in, and falling with each breath out. You don't need to change anything. The breath knows its own way. Just notice how it moves, slow and steady, like the waves we watched by Nora's window, arriving and leaving all on their own.

Picture a soft wool blanket, folded over the arm of a chair, glowing in the light of a small lamp. That's how your body can feel now. Warm. Heavy. Soft at the edges. Resting exactly where it is, with nowhere to go and nothing to hold up. Just being, quietly, in a warm room at the end of the day.

Now the belly. Let it be soft. There's no need to hold it in, no need to hold it tight. Let it rise when you breathe in and fall when you breathe out, round and easy. Sometimes we carry our worries here, in a small knot. If there's one tonight, imagine it slowly loosening, like a ribbon being untied.

Feel your back, resting against the bed. The upper back, between the shoulder blades. The middle back. The lower back. Let all of it sink down a little further, as if the bed were slowly rising up to meet you and hold you. You don't need to support yourself at all. You are completely held.

Let the heaviness spread to your hips. Let them settle into the mattress, wide and warm and still. All day, they've carried you from one place to another, sitting, standing, walking. Now they can rest. There's nowhere they need to take you. Let them be heavy, and let that heaviness feel like relief.

Now let the warmth move slowly down through your legs. The thighs, long and heavy. The knees, softening. The calves, letting go of every last bit of effort. The ankles, loose and easy. Imagine a slow, warm wave travelling all the way down, leaving everything it touches calm and still behind it.

And finally, the feet. Notice the soles, the heels, the toes. Feet carry us through every day, and they're the part of us we notice least. Let them rest now. Let the toes uncurl. Let the feet feel warm and heavy, at the very end of a long, slow journey from head to toe.

Now, let your attention widen, to hold the whole body all at once. From the top of your head to the tips of your toes. Warm, heavy, still, resting. Every part of you supported by the bed beneath you. Nothing to hold up. Nothing to carry. Just a whole body, breathing slowly, at rest in the dark.

Earlier tonight, we talked about savouring. About slowing down to really notice a good moment while it's happening. This is one of those moments. A warm bed. A quiet room. A body at rest. If you like, let yourself savour it, just a little. Not to make it last. Just to enjoy it while it's here.

Here's one last thought for this part of the night. This moment is enough. It doesn't need to lead anywhere. It doesn't need to become anything better. A body at rest, a slow breath, a quiet room. Enough, just as it is. And when it passes, as everything does, another gentle moment will come.

Let yourself drift a little deeper now. If thoughts come along, let them float past like clouds over the sea at night, dark and soft and slow. You don't need to follow them. Just let the warmth and the heaviness carry you, gently, gently, closer and closer to sleep.

Remember the quiet house we walked through at the start, turning off the lights one room at a time. By now, almost every light is out. The head, the face, the shoulders, the arms, the belly, the legs, the feet. All of them dark and warm and still. Only a soft glow remains, somewhere near the heart, steady and calm, keeping you company as you drift toward sleep.
